title: Solve a whole problem for users
locator: Why it is important; What it means
claim: Scope services around user needs and coherent journeys, while improving incrementally.
context: Public services crossing teams and channels.
limitations: Normative service standard; not comparative causal evidence.

title: Structuring forms
locator: Know why you are asking every question; Start with one thing per page
claim: Justify collected information; start with task units and merge when research supports repeated expert work.
context: Digital public-service forms.
limitations: Does not determine an optimal screen count for commerce or all forms.

title: Question pages
locator: How it works; Asking multiple questions on a page; passport example
claim: Related questions may share a page; field purpose, headings, back navigation and answer reuse matter.
context: Public-service transactional forms.
limitations: Examples inspected as documentation, not executed.

title: Check answers
locator: When to use; Let users go back and change their answers
claim: Review placement scales with transaction size; correction links should preserve answers and identify their target.
context: Applications and information submission.
limitations: Not evidence that every low-risk action needs a confirmation screen.

title: Empty states
locator: Anatomy; Types of empty states; Visual guidelines for smaller empty spaces
claim: Different causes of absence need different guidance; imagery and primary actions are optional.
context: Enterprise dashboards, tables, tiles and panels.
limitations: House-system layout details are not universal standards.

title: Beyond the five-user assumption: Benefits of increased sample sizes in usability testing
locator: pp.379–382, Method, Results and Analyses, Tables 1–2, Discussion
claim: Small samples varied substantially in known-problem discovery in one timesheet task.
context: 60 users across three experience groups; 100 resamples per size; 45 known problems.
limitations: Finite observed problem set, one application/task; cannot guarantee general discovery percentages.

title: Why You Only Need to Test with 5 Users
evidence_type: expert cost-benefit guidance based on discovery model
locator: Iterative Design; When To Test More Users
claim: The recommendation concerns repeated formative rounds and comparable users; distinct user groups require additional coverage.
context: Budget allocation for iterative usability improvement.
limitations: Model averages do not prove a particular sample finds a fixed fraction of problems.

title: Can There Ever Be Too Many Options? A Meta-Analytic Review of Choice Overload
locator: pp.412–414 Method; pp.417–419 moderator analysis and Discussion
claim: Near-zero pooled effect coexists with substantial heterogeneity; a universal less-choice rule is unsupported.
context: 63 conditions from 50 published/unpublished experiments, N=5036.
limitations: 2000–2009 experiments; mixed outcomes and contexts; seven approximate nonsignificant effects coded zero.

title: Choice overload: A conceptual review and meta-analysis
locator: pp.339–340 Method; pp.344–348 Results; pp.352–353 Prior meta-analytic research; Appendix B
claim: Task difficulty, choice complexity, preference uncertainty and decision goal moderate assortment effects.
context: 99 observations from 53 published studies in 21 articles, N=7202.
limitations: Different inclusion/model choices from 2010 analysis; not a universal option-count threshold; corrigendum inspected.

title: Corrigendum to Choice overload
locator: Corrections to page 348
claim: Corrects coefficient and test-statistic notation in three reported comparisons.
context: Companion to UX-09.
limitations: Not an independent replication or new experiment.

title: Web Page Design: Implications of Memory, Structure and Scent for Information Retrieval
locator: pp.27–30 Methods, Results, Discussion, Implications for design
claim: Two-level structures beat the tested deeper hierarchy; broadest was not significantly faster than moderate breadth.
context: 19 experienced users; Encarta categories; 512 leaf nodes; paper task reference.
limitations: 1998 desktop artificial task; non-target contents differed; cannot prescribe modern navigation item counts.

title: A Predictive Model of Menu Performance
locator: pp.627–628 model; pp.630–632 calibration; Evaluating the model with real designs
claim: Menu performance combines search, pointing and learned location, rather than option count alone.
context: Calibration used eight right-handed graduate CS students and familiar/unfamiliar/static/random menus.
limitations: Narrow population; mathematical model is not a general law of arbitrary screen complexity; full evaluation-result sections incompletely fetched.

title: The Magical Number Seven, Plus or Minus Two
locator: Absolute judgment; The span of immediate memory; Recoding; conclusion
claim: Discusses information processing and memory chunks, not a universal on-screen menu limit.
context: 1956 psychology review, university-hosted transcription.
limitations: Historical tasks and constructs; later working-memory literature not comprehensively reviewed.

title: Request runtime permissions
locator: Basic principles; Workflow for requesting permissions; Handle permission denial
claim: Request in task context, allow cancellation and degrade appropriately after refusal.
context: Android runtime permissions with OS/version-specific behavior.
limitations: Does not empirically measure this product's consent quality or justify repeated persuasion.

title: Android Permissions Remystified: A Field Study on Contextual Integrity
locator: §3 Methodology, §3.3 Exit Survey; §5.1–5.2 expectations and blocking
claim: Data-access expectations and task relevance matter; retrospective permission preferences vary with context.
context: 36 adults, one-week instrumented phones; exit questions on sampled requests.
limitations: 2015 platform and retrospective stated choices; 27M logged accesses are not 27M user judgments.

title: Personal names around the world
locator: Scenarios; Examples of differences; Implications for field design
claim: Name components, order and address conventions vary; field decisions depend on application needs.
context: Global web forms and data models.
limitations: Introductory guidance, not exhaustive cultural authority or empirical form comparison.

title: Text-Free User Interfaces for Illiterate and Semi-Literate Users
evidence_type: ethnographic design and exploratory prototype studies
locator: §II–IV context/design; §VII experimental setup and qualitative results
claim: Locally tested graphics, native-language audio and consistent help supported particular first-time users.
context: Bangalore communities; over 180 hours of engagement; small prototype tests.
limitations: Exploratory small samples; authors state quantitative results not statistically significant; no universal icon vocabulary.
version: ICTD 2006 manuscript; do not conflate with expanded 2007 journal version

title: Designing Mobile Interfaces for Novice and Low-Literacy Users
locator: Table I; §4.2–4.5 banking prototypes, setup/results; §5 health-entry study; §6
claim: Completion, speed and assistance can favor different modalities; voice familiarity does not ensure universal success.
context: 58 banking participants in India; 13 health-entry participants; cross-country ethnographic background.
limitations: First-use tasks, feature phones, Wizard-of-Oz speech; experimenter prompts permitted and assistance differed; no unassisted-success inference.

title: The science behind Duolingo's home screen redesign
locator: Quick overview; The science behind the changes; FAQ on labels, progress, review and long scrolling
claim: A guided path bundles sequencing, practice and content changes and retains some revisit routes.
context: 2022 tree-to-path redesign.
limitations: Product rationale and feature description; not a randomized layout-only outcome study.

title: Duolingo Path Meets Expectations for Proficiency Outcomes
locator: §1.1 changes; §2.1 participants; §3.1.1 historical proficiency comparisons (printed pp.6–7); §4.1 Discussion
claim: Measured selected course completers; historical comparisons are explicitly tentative.
context: 165 Spanish and 92 French adult learners completing A2 content; 2023 data window.
limitations: No randomized navigation-only comparison; completion selection, content changes and different proficiency tests.

title: Inside the redesigned Figma, where your work takes center stage
locator: Clearing the stage; Prioritizing features; An interface for usability, not decoration
claim: Designers balanced newcomer comprehension with professional muscle memory, retaining several familiar arrangements.
context: UI3 initial redesign rationale.
limitations: Internal test methods and effect sizes undisclosed.

title: Figma on Figma: Our approach to designing UI3
locator: Docked panels; Blend modes; Properties panel
claim: Several minimal-looking controls were reversed after workflow costs appeared.
context: Post-beta UI3 iteration in a high-frequency professional tool.
limitations: No public controlled dataset or quantified causal estimates; historical example, not live-app audit.

title: Checkout Optimization: 5 Ways to Minimize Form Fields in Checkout
locator: Why form fields matter more than steps; Five ways to minimize visible form fields
claim: Visible field burden and relevance are more informative than step count alone.
context: Consumer commerce usability research and benchmark.
limitations: Underlying premium observations/data not fully inspected; descriptive benchmark is not a causal A/B test.

title: One-Page Checkout Benefits and Optimization Tips
evidence_type: vendor guidance and selected customer case claims
locator: One-page checkout features; Benefits; B2B; How to measure; FAQ
claim: Both one- and three-page configurations are described; claims of gains include bundled checkout capabilities.
context: Shopify commerce platform.
limitations: Promotional source; reported merchant lift lacks inspected randomization details; do not generalize layout-only causality.

title: Measuring the User Experience on a Large Scale: User-Centered Metrics for Web Applications
locator: Related Work; PULSE/HEART; Goals–Signals–Metrics
claim: Choose metrics from user goals and triangulate logs with research; activity metrics can be ambiguous.
context: Large-scale web products.
limitations: Framework experience report, not proof every metric family should be mandatory; author PDF followed through official publication link.

title: Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction
locator: Table 1; §3–6 development/validation; §7 Discussion & Future Work
claim: Expectation-setting, dismissal, correction and cautious adaptation are inspectable interaction concerns.
context: 18 guidelines assessed by practitioners on AI-infused products.
limitations: Relevance/clarity evaluation, not causal proof of user outcomes; pre-generative-agent context and stated domain gaps.

title: Dark Patterns at Scale: Findings from a Crawl of 11K Shopping Websites
evidence_type: empirical web measurement and expert classification
locator: §3 taxonomy; §4 method; §5 examples; §6.4 limitations
claim: Interface patterns can distort informed choice; prevalence measured only within a bounded text-based crawl.
context: Shopping product pages and simulated purchase flows.
limitations: Does not estimate persuasion effects or contemporary prevalence; visual/account-dependent patterns undercovered.

title: Creating an experience map
locator: When to use experience mapping; Identify common stages; Live with the map
claim: Maps should follow researched experiences; different stages may require separate maps.
context: Long, multi-person, multi-channel services.
limitations: Does not justify inventing persona feelings or mapping every small interaction.

title: Map and understand a user's whole problem
locator: Introduction; Service landscape; User perspective; Work out what to change
claim: User experience and backstage delivery views answer different questions; map at a suitable organizational level.
context: Cross-organizational public services.
limitations: Not every feature team can or should map an entire service landscape.

title: Onboarding
locator: JS placeholder; linked onboarding.md rejected by web tool
claim: No recommendation relied upon from inaccessible body.
context: Native app onboarding.
limitations: Search excerpts discovered; body unavailable in this lane. Shell fetch also failed DNS.

title: On the Rate of Gain of Information
locator: Search discovery; university PDF route returned 404
claim: No detailed result used; follow original method before teaching as a general law.
context: Choice-reaction tasks.
limitations: Full original not inspected; do not treat menu-model citation as original-paper reading.

title: Direct Manipulation: A Step Beyond Programming Languages
locator: Repeated PDF timeouts
claim: No detailed conclusion relied upon from unavailable full paper.
context: Direct manipulation.
limitations: Search excerpts only; omitted from core evidence count.

title: The prevention of mode errors through sensory feedback
locator: Official abstract; linked CiteSeer PDF returned 403
claim: Abstract reports two text-editing mode-feedback experiments.
context: Keyboard and foot-pedal maintained modes.
limitations: Full methods not inspected; excluded from quantitative synthesis.
